name: Project Handbook
one_liner: How this project will be run — approach, processes, rules, roles.
purpose: The Project Handbook summarises the project objectives and documents the selected approach for achieving the project goals. It documents the Critical Success Factors, the key controlling processes, the conflict resolution and escalation procedure, policies, rules and mindsets. It also documents the governance roles and their responsibilities and defines which plans are needed, including any PM² tailoring decisions.

fields.what: Executive summary of the project, or simply links to the Business Case and Project Charter documents.

fields.what: The management lifecycle (phases) used, how the project moves between phases (approvals/gates), and any deviation from standard PM².

fields.what: Table listing each artefact with Yes/No, its location, and, if No, why. Complexity, risk and PSC influence the choice.

fields.what: Other domain methodologies (e.g. Agile for IT) or standards that must be considered when planning and applying PM² processes.

fields.what: Agreed “rules of conduct” on team interaction, communication, meetings, collaboration and contractors that the methodology does not cover.
fields.who: PM drafts from Kick-off MoM · team agrees

fields.what: How conflicts are resolved or escalated, plus the impact-based escalation ladder and tolerances referenced by every Management Plan.
fields.castor: Very low/low decided by PCT; medium by PM and Grace Hopper at the status meeting; high/very high by PSC.

fields.what: High-level risk process: identification, assessment (likelihood × impact), response development (avoid/transfer/reduce/accept) and control at status meetings.
fields.castor: Risks logged in the Risk Log by the PM; R-07 “Levallois loses its key architect” reviewed at every status meeting.

fields.what: High-level issue process: identification, assessment and action recommendation, actions implementation, and weekly issue control.
fields.castor: When R-07 materialised it left the Risk Log and became an issue in the Issue Log, with remediation actions logged.

fields.what: Specify, evaluate, approve, monitor implementation and validate requirements; a fuller Requirements Management Plan may be created instead.
fields.castor: Requirements specified with Ada Lovelace (BA), approved by Florence Nightingale, validated by Marie Curie before acceptance.

fields.what: Change identification (Change Request Form), assessment of impact, approval via the escalation path, implementation in the Work Plan, weekly control.
fields.who: PM owns · PSC approves high impact
fields.castor: The verbal “add SRF-backstop screens” request from a Board member’s cabinet was routed through a Change Request Form to the PSC.

fields.what: Define quality characteristics, perform quality assurance, quality control (Quality Review Checklist), deliverables acceptance and final acceptance.

fields.castor: Quality assurance performed by W. Edwards Deming (PQA) independently of the PM; Quality Review Report produced quarterly.

fields.castor: PSC monthly, chaired by Florence Nightingale; Project Status Meeting every two weeks; monthly contractor report from Gustave Eiffel.

fields.what: Define acceptance criteria, perform acceptance activities, obtain provisional/final formal approval from the Project Owner for each deliverable.
fields.castor: Acceptance signed by Florence Nightingale; the reconciliation report was only partially accepted after Marie Curie’s objection.

fields.what: Summary of the move from project mode to operations: transition goals, transition activities and transition schedule; or a link to the Transition Plan.
fields.who: PM drafts · PSC accountable for Manage Transition

fields.what: Impact on processes, people and culture; implementation strategy, change activities and benefits tracking; or a link to the Business Implementation Plan.

fields.castor: Project Status Report every two weeks; Project Progress Report at review meetings; Levallois contractor status report monthly.

fields.castor: Phase-exit Review, Quality Review, Deliverables Acceptance, Transition, Business Implementation and Stakeholders Checklists all retained.

fields.castor: PO Florence Nightingale, SP Leonardo da Vinci, BM Grace Hopper, UR Marie Curie, CPM Gustave Eiffel; Agile roles deleted.

fields.castor: Business Case and Project Charter (24 Mar 2026), Planning Kick-off MoM (09 Apr 2026), Project Work Plan v1.0.

traps: Handbook is approved by the PO (A), not the PSC — classic.
The six Management Plans are part of the Handbook, not rivals to it.
Handbook = how the project is run; Work Plan = what work, when, how much.
Scope and objectives come from the Charter; the Handbook does not redefine them.
It is a living document, updated all the way to Closing — not a one-off Planning output.
